misconceptions.description: Assigning a quality rating to the prototype without naming which rubric criterion or heuristic the rating is tied to
misconceptions.trigger: review says 'navigation: 4 out of 5' with no criterion or evidence cited
misconceptions.feedback: Tie every score to a named criterion and the screen evidence that earned it, so the rating is reproducible.

misconceptions.description: Rating a prototype highly because it looks finished, even when instructional alignment or accessibility criteria fail
misconceptions.trigger: high overall score driven by visual appeal while objectives-to-assessment alignment is unchecked
misconceptions.feedback: Score instructional and accessibility criteria independently of visual polish; a beautiful screen can still fail alignment.

misconceptions.description: Listing all quality issues as equal so a defense cannot tell which problems block readiness from which are cosmetic
misconceptions.trigger: issue log treats a broken assessment and a misaligned margin as the same priority
misconceptions.feedback: Rate each issue by severity and effect on the learner, so high-severity blockers are clearly separated from cosmetic items.

misconceptions.description: Treating an AI's overall quality score for the prototype as the final review verdict instead of a checklist to verify
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports 'the AI rated my prototype 9 out of 10' as the quality finding
misconceptions.feedback: Use an AI review as a candidate issue list to confirm against the rubric and the live prototype; the score is not the verdict.
